correctness.rationale: The primary curve has unique cusp at [0:1:0] and unique tangent Z=0, so every geometric projective stabilizer fixes both and acts affinely by x->Ax+C, y->Dx+By+E. The primary parametrization t->(t^q,t^(q+2)+t) identifies the affine curve with A1, whose automorphism must be t->at+b. Comparing x yields A=a^q, C=b^q. In char2, (at+b)^(q+2) contains exponents q+2,q,2,0. The t² coefficient b^q a² has no left-hand mate when q>=4, forcing b=0. Remaining coefficients give B=a and a^(q+1)=1, D=C=E=0. Conversely these diagonals preserve the equation; odd q+1 has simple roots. Independent parity expansion checks q=4..256 verified every relevant exponent, finite confirmation of a universal coefficient argument.

originality.rationale: Kollar 2026 builds the characteristic-two rational plane-curve family and proves its affine normalization and unique double cusp; he does not state this exact geometric PGL3 stabilizer in the inspected primary text. Full stabilizer of a fixed embedding is strictly more constrained than Aut(A1), and unrelated known stabilizers of other cuspidal curves cannot imply it. Novelty is best-of-knowledge and excludes group scheme or abstract curve automorphisms.
residual_risks: Only geometric points are classified; infinitesimal nonreduced stabilizer scheme and abstract automorphisms are outside scope.
A specialized earlier classification of the original equation under another name might exist.

value.rationale: The exact projective symmetry group and obstruction to translations are a natural invariant distinguishing this unusual large-degree positive-characteristic embedded curve from its highly symmetric affine normalization. An infinite-parameter complete group classification is independently useful.

final_claim: Over algebraic closure of F2, for q=2^n with n>=2, plane curve Z^2 Y^q=X^(q+2)+XZ^(q+1) has exactly q+1 projective linear k-rational stabilizers, represented by diag(u^q,u,1) with u^(q+1)=1; the group is cyclic and no nontrivial affine-normalization translation extends projectively.
